operations_plan.summary: Establish the filler location on the upper radiator tank and remove the existing top-center cap-like protrusion so it can be replaced by a complete filler-neck assembly.

steps.description: Inspect the upper radiator rail and the existing top-center protrusion. Use the cylindrical or rotational center of face 798 to establish the filler axis, located at approximately z=0 and y=181.4 mm. Set the axis normal to the upper tank and parallel to +Y. Project this axis and the protrusion footprint onto a construction plane tangent to the highest upper-tank surface. The exact upper support face is not uniquely identified in model.json; therefore select it geometrically from solid 0 as the uppermost face in feature_01_03 whose outward normal is predominantly +Y and whose projected region contains the face-798 axis.

Measure the existing protrusion diameter, upper-tank thickness in the front-to-back X direction, and available clearance to the tank edges. No filler dimensions were specified in the request, so define proportional parameters from this geometry: neck outer diameter based on the existing protrusion seat, neck inner diameter sized to leave a uniform structural wall, neck height sufficient to expose a pour opening above the rail, and cap diameter slightly larger than the neck lip. Constrain all new circular geometry concentric with the axis established in step 1.

Remove or suppress the existing top-center cap-like feature represented by face 798 and its containing solid, expected to be solid 19. If it is a separate body, delete only that body. If it is fused to the upper tank, remove it with a local delete-face/heal or a bounded cut that restores the underlying upper-tank surface without changing the surrounding upper rail. Preserve the two diagonal isolation mounts represented by faces 796 and 797.

Create a clean local mounting pad for the filler neck only if the restored upper-tank surface is curved or blended. Sketch a circle concentric with the filler axis and form a shallow additive pad or locally planar boss that remains fully inside the upper rail width in X. Blend the pad into solid 0 with a small tangent fillet, avoiding the chamfered upper ends and preserving the original radiator envelope everywhere outside the filler region.

operations_plan.summary: Create an integrated raised pouring neck and a true fill passage into the upper radiator tank.

steps.description: On the prepared upper-tank pad or tangent plane, sketch two concentric circles about the established +Y filler axis. Use the derived neck outer and inner diameters from operation_01_step_02. Fully constrain the sketch to z=0 and to the X coordinate of the existing top-center feature so the new filler remains centered through the tank thickness and does not shift toward either radiator face.

Extrude the annular sketch upward along +Y to form the principal cylindrical filler neck. Extend its lower end sufficiently into or onto the upper tank to guarantee a positive overlap, then boolean-union the neck with radiator solid 0. Keep the neck height visually proportionate to the existing cap feature and high enough that the pouring lip and removable cap clear the top rail.

Create the pouring mouth by revolving an axial section around the +Y filler axis. Form a short outward flare or rounded entry lip at the upper end of the neck, with a smooth lead-in from the opening and an external annular seat for the cap. Use tangent arcs and a small edge radius to eliminate sharp pouring edges. Keep the maximum lip diameter inside the available upper-tank clearance measured in operation_01_step_02.

Cut the concentric internal fill passage through the neck and through the upper-tank wall. Terminate the cut at the detected internal tank cavity so the opening communicates with the coolant volume. If the source body contains no modeled internal cavity, infer a consistent tank wall thickness from nearby shell geometry and create a localized internal manifold void beneath the neck rather than leaving a blind decorative hole. Do not allow the cut to break through the front or rear tank walls, radiator core face, or lower surface of the upper rail.

Add small fillets at the neck-to-tank junction and at exposed lip edges. Maintain a larger root radius externally for stress reduction while keeping the internal passage unobstructed. Verify that the union is watertight, the neck has uniform minimum wall thickness, and no new geometry intersects the radiator fins, fan guards, or the opposite branded face.

operations_plan.summary: Create a distinct removable cap that seats concentrically on the new filler neck and closes the pouring passage.

steps.description: Create an axial cap-section sketch on a plane passing through the +Y filler axis. Project the finished neck lip, outer seating diameter, and upper sealing face into the sketch. Because no attachment method or pressure rating was specified, use a generic removable cap with a cylindrical internal socket, an annular sealing shoulder, and a shallow retaining bead or friction-fit relief rather than assuming a detailed threaded or pressure-rated bayonet standard.

Revolve the cap section 360 degrees around the filler axis as a new, separate solid. Form a closed top wall, depending side skirt, internal neck recess, and annular underside sealing land. Derive radial and axial clearances from the neck dimensions so the cap does not boolean-union with solid 0 and can be removed in the +Y direction. Maintain adequate cap wall thickness and make its outside diameter larger than the pouring lip for visual and manual accessibility.

Add an annular sealing feature inside the cap, represented by either a shallow gasket groove or a compliant seal seat concentric with the neck. Position it to contact the flat annular surface of the pouring lip when the cap is fully seated. Keep this feature representational unless a separate gasket material or pressure specification is supplied.

Refine the cap exterior with a rounded or shallow flared top profile consistent with the existing black radiator hardware. Add a circumferential grip rim or evenly patterned grip ribs if sufficient clearance exists. Apply small fillets to all hand-contact edges while preserving a distinct part boundary between the cap and filler neck.

Place the cap in its closed position using a concentric constraint to the filler axis and a coincident or offset seating constraint between the cap sealing land and neck lip. Confirm that the cap can be translated away along +Y without collision after disengaging the retaining fit. Retain the cap as an independent solid or component to communicate removability.

operations_plan.summary: Validate the completed filling system and preserve all unrelated radiator, fan, hose, branding, and mounting geometry.

steps.description: Run body-validity and interference checks. Confirm that the filler neck is joined only to radiator solid 0, the cap remains a separate removable body, and the fill passage is open from the pouring mouth into the upper-tank coolant region. Check for zero-thickness edges, self-intersections, and unintended openings in the upper rail.

Compare the edited model against the original envelope outside the localized top-center area. Verify that the finned core and branding, faces 0-14, both seven-blade fan rotors and guards, the central rear separator, side hose barbs on faces 794 and 795, and isolation mounts on faces 796 and 797 are unchanged. Confirm adequate clearance between the cap and surrounding vehicle-mount features.

Assign the integrated neck and passage to a new filling-system section associated with the upper radiator tank, and assign the removable cap as a separate feature and solid within that section. Preserve the original semantic orientation: +Y is top, +X is back, -X is front, +Z is right, and -Z is left.
